findings.title: PrInputs/PrFacts contract cannot feed the title and "why" prose
findings.description:
Task 9's `PrFacts` carries the slice design *path*, the task items, and the review path, verdict and sha. Three consumers need more than that:
- **Task 10a** needs the design's H1 to build the title.
- **Task 11** needs design content to write "Why" prose. A path alone gives the model nothing to summarize, and D3 says it is "given PrFacts only".
- **Task 8** reads only `reviewedSha`, but `PrFacts` also carries the review's verdict. No task says where the verdict is read.

Also, `PrInputs` is never defined. Task 7 builds the commit and slice halves of `gather_inputs` and Task 8 adds the review scan, but no task composes them into `gather_inputs -> PrInputs`.

Add the design text (or H1) and the review verdict to `PrInputs`/`PrFacts`. Assign the `gather_inputs` composition and the `PrInputs` dataclass to Task 7 or 8.

findings.title: No task provides the local head sha that Task 6 requires
findings.description: `check_head_pushed` takes `local_sha`, and Task 13 must supply it. Task 3 adds only `current_branch` and `commits_in_range`. `git_utils.py` has a private `_resolve_rev(ref, cwd)` (line 339), which returns `None` on failure. The task should either name a public local-sha helper or say to reuse `_resolve_rev`. If it does, a `None` result must raise rather than silently pass the "behind" check.

findings.title: body.py accumulates four tasks and will exceed the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: Tasks 10, 10a, 11 and 12 all write to `src/squadron/pr/body.py`. Together they add the model composer, title resolution (including H1 parsing and fallbacks), the section-definition table and `compose_body`, and the presence check. With their tests, that is likely over the file-size guideline and mixes several responsibilities. Split into separate modules, for example `composer.py`, `title.py` and `body.py` (sections plus check). Task 10 already names the composer as injectable, so the split costs little.

findings.title: Task 16.4 lists a merge as a task item, against the project's git rules
findings.description:
CLAUDE.md says to never write a merge or push as a task, sub-item or success criterion in a task file. Merging happens in Phase 7, after code review passes. Remove the "Merge `385-slice...` into `squadron-pr`" item.

The "Ask the Project Manager how they want it run" line is a PM-confirmation step with no named rule behind it. The project rules call such steps invalid, so reduce that item to "code review is required".

findings.title: Task 5 contradicts itself on an unreachable `cf`
findings.description: The bullet opens with "Do not degrade an unreachable `cf` to a default base" and then says that when `cf` is unavailable the chain proceeds to the host default. Task 5.2 and the design both intend the second behavior. A junior implementer could read the opening sentence as requiring a refusal. Reword it to "an unreachable `cf` means the integration-branch term is absent; it does not substitute a guessed branch".

findings.title: "First commit's subject" is ambiguous given newest-first ordering
findings.description: Task 3 returns commits newest first. Task 10a's fallback uses "the first commit's subject", which a junior would read as `commits[0]`, the tip commit. Say which commit is meant: the tip or the oldest.

findings.title: Identity precondition has no implementing sub-item
findings.description: Task 13.1 orders "identity, then pushed" and Task 13.2 tests the refusal. No task states how the hostname for `identify_operator(hostname)` is obtained, or that the call is wired into `create`. A line in 13.1 would cover it, since the locator presumably carries the host.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage and test-with sequencing
findings.description:
These design criteria map to tasks:
- **Base selection and refusal:** Task 5.
- **Push precondition:** Task 6.
- **Merged-ancestor review exclusion:** Task 8.2.
- **Five-section contract and presence check:** Tasks 11 and 12.
- **Title rules:** Task 10a.
- **Dry-run equality:** Task 13.2.
- **Timeouts and failure matrix across five call sites:** Task 14.
- **Provider failure:** Task 10.2.
- **Import boundary:** Task 15.1.
- **Docstring correction:** Task 15.2.
- **Checkbox parser with a real-file fixture:** Task 2.2.
- **Live evidence and zero pyright errors:** Task 16.

Each implementation task is followed by its test task. The task order matches the design's order. The task file has no `**Commit**:` markers, which is acceptable. No NFR is restated in the slice, so no load-test or CI-wiring task is required.
